title: Optically Induced Thermal Runaway in Phase-Change VO2 Nanostructures
authors: Jiří Kabát, Peter Kepič, Andrea Konečná, Filip Ligmajer
abstract: While thermal runaway occurs across diverse physical disciplines, its presence in subwavelength phase-change photonics remains unexplored because existing thermo-optical models break down near sharp optical transitions. Here, we introduce an iterative multiphysics framework coupling full-wave electrodynamics with heat transfer, and we discover optically induced thermal runaway in vanadium dioxide (VO2) nanostructures. The runaway switching threshold depends on the illumination wavelength, ambient temperature, and underlying substrate, with external thermal biasing significantly reducing the optical intensity required for runaway ignition. Our results push forward the modeling of sharp photothermal transitions and provide essential design principles for active metasurfaces, neuromorphic photonic devices, and nanoscale thermal management.
summary: This work develops an iterative multiphysics model to study thermal runaway in VO2 nanostructures undergoing a phase transition. By coupling electrodynamics and heat transfer, the authors predict that the runaway threshold is highly sensitive to external factors like ambient temperature and substrate properties. This provides crucial design principles for active photonic devices.
main_problem: The paper investigates optically induced thermal runaway in phase-change VO2 nanostructures, addressing the failure of existing models near sharp optical transitions.
main_result: Thermal runaway is predicted, showing that the ignition threshold depends on wavelength, ambient temperature, and substrate; preheating significantly lowers the required optical intensity.
method: An iterative multiphysics framework is introduced, coupling full-wave electrodynamics with steady-state heat transfer calculations.
model_or_system: The system involves VO2 nanostructures exhibiting an insulator-metal transition (IMT) and strong temperature-dependent optical properties. The model iteratively solves for the temperature change ($\Delta T$) by coupling absorbed power ($\dot{Q}$) to heat transfer.
key_observables: Thermal runaway behavior, required optical intensity for ignition (ITR), and steady-state temperature maps.
important_parameters: Illumination wavelength ($\lambda_{	ext{exc}}$), incident intensity ($I_{	ext{inc}}$), ambient temperature ($T_0$), and substrate thermal conductivity ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The model requires iterative calculations because the change in temperature significantly alters the material's dielectric function, invalidating one-step approximations.
figures_summary: Figures show parametric maps of steady-state temperature dependence on wavelength and intensity, confirming step-like runaway signatures. Other figures compare heating on different substrates, highlighting the dominant role of substrate thermal conductivity.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the multiphysics framework, demonstrates the runaway effect in free-standing structures, and then systematically analyzes how the surrounding substrate (via $\kappa$ and $\epsilon$) modifies the thermal runaway threshold and steady-state temperature profiles.
why_interesting: The strong, non-linear, and temperature-dependent nature of the optical absorption coefficient ($\sigma_{	ext{abs}}(T)$) driving the thermal runaway mechanism shares conceptual links with non-equilibrium phase transitions studied in statistical mechanics.
